diag_down: No connection — your router or provider is down
diag_dns: Websites can't be found — name lookup (DNS) is failing
diag_http: Web pages are blocked — maybe a Wi-Fi login page is in the way
diag_partial: Some checks are failing — the connection is unstable
diag_lan: Can't reach your router — check Wi-Fi or the cable
diag_isp: Your router is fine — the outage is at your provider (ISP)
chart_empty: Response time appears here after the first checks
targets_empty: Results appear after the first check
events_empty: No events yet — that's good news
ins_coverage_low_t: Only {pct}% of the time was monitored
ins_coverage_low_d: Gaps weaken your evidence. Keep this computer awake and plugged in, or run Internet Monitor on a small device that stays on all the time, like a Raspberry Pi (see the Raspberry Pi guide on the website).
ins_provider_route_t: {n} outages stopped right after your router
ins_provider_route_d: Your router answered but nothing beyond it did. That points at the provider's side, which is exactly what a complaint needs to show.
ins_line_sync_t: The line itself dropped during {n} outages
ins_line_sync_d: Your router reported that the line to the provider was down. That's a fault on the provider's line, not in your home, and it's the strongest point for a complaint.
ins_snr_low_t: Your line's noise margin is low ({db} dB)
ins_snr_low_d: Below 6 dB a DSL line drops easily. This is measured by your router, it's a fault on the provider's line, and it's a strong point for a complaint: ask them to check the line.
ins_provider_dropped_t: The provider cut your internet connection {n} times
ins_provider_dropped_d: Your line stayed up, but the router recorded that the provider itself closed the connection. That's on the provider's side, and the report shows each time.
ins_router_restarts_d: A router that restarts by itself is often overheating or losing power. Check its power adapter and give it some air. If it keeps happening, ask the provider to replace it.
ins_quota_pace_t: At this pace your data runs out before the month ends
ins_quota_pace_d: You've used {pct}% of your plan with {days} days to go. Heavy downloads, updates and video in HD use the most.
rt_sub: Read from your router on your home network
rt_web_wrong_password: The router rejected the password, so the app stopped trying. Fix it in Settings → App.
rt_web_busy: Someone is signed in to the router's page, so the app will try again in a few minutes.
rt_web_unsupported: This router's page isn't one the app can read yet, so only the UPnP details are shown.
rt_web_unreachable: The router's page didn't answer. The app will try again in a few minutes.
rt_not_found: No router answered. To see the line state and your data usage here, turn on UPnP (a router feature that lets apps ask it for its status) in the router's settings (often under Network or Advanced). Some provider routers don't offer it.
rt_no_counters: This router doesn't share its traffic counters over UPnP. Add the router's password in Settings → App to track your data plan from its page.
rt_pace_over: {days} days left. At this pace you'll use about {projected}.
rt_pace_ok: {days} days left. At this pace your data lasts the month.
ins_dns_failures_d: The line was up but website names couldn't be looked up. Changing your DNS (the internet's address book) to 1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8 in the router or in Windows network settings usually fixes this, and it's worth telling the provider.
ins_peak_hours_t: {pct}% of the downtime falls between {from}:00 and {to}:00
ins_peak_hours_d: Outages cluster at the same time of day, which often means the provider's network is overloaded at those hours. Mention the time window in your complaint.
ins_bufferbloat_d: Calls and games lag when someone downloads. Turning on SQM or QoS in the router usually fixes it; if the router has no such option, ask the provider.
ins_weak_wifi_d: Move closer to the router, or measure over a cable. The provider can blame weak Wi-Fi for drops, so a cable makes your evidence stronger.
ins_use_cable_d: For a complaint, measure over a cable to the router so the provider can't blame the Wi-Fi.
ins_power_cuts_d: They are left out of the compensation estimate. A small UPS (a battery backup) for the router keeps the internet up during short power cuts.
ins_slow_vs_plan_t: Your speed is {pct}% of what you pay for
ins_slow_vs_plan_d: Your speed tests show far less than your plan. That is a valid complaint on its own, and the report has the numbers.
ins_slow_evenings_t: Evenings are much slower ({peak} vs {offpeak} Mbps)
ins_slow_evenings_d: The speed drops between 7pm and midnight, a sign of an overloaded network. Run tests at both times so the report shows the difference.
ins_file_complaint_t: {n} outages in {days} days and no complaint yet
ins_file_complaint_d: The Complaints page has the text and the evidence ready to send.
ins_all_good_t: No outages in the last {days} days
ins_all_good_d: Everything looks fine. Keep the app running so you have proof if things change.
